newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Father calls Cunanan bookworm who shunned violence.
newsitem.headline: Father calls Cunanan bookworm who shunned violence.

text.p: Andrew Cunanan, found dead in an apparent suicide after Miami Beach police cornered him over the murder of fashion king Gianni Versace, was a gentle book-lover who shunned violence, his Filipino father said on Thursday.

In a telephone interview with Manila's ABS-CBN television network, Modesto Cunanan laughed off reports that his son was a homosexual and described him as a person of discriminating tastes who could "talk his way out of a situation".
The elder Cunanan was speaking to ABS-CBN from an undisclosed location. He left his home in nearby Plaridel town last week after the news of his son's suspected involvement in Versace's death.

Modesto Cunanan, who worked for the U.S. Navy in the United States, said he last saw his son in 1988 when Andrew came to visit him in this small town just north of Manila, but the young Cunanan stayed only a few weeks.
"Basically, what he did was grab a book and sit in an air-conditioned restaurant... He spent the rest of the afternoon sitting there," the father said.

"All his childhood years I never heard him getting involved in any kind of scuffle or fistfight, a very peaceful guy. If he can talk his way out of a situation, he would do it. He's not going to resort to violence."

Versace, who dressed the world's beautiful people in flamboyant and sexy couture, was shot and killed on July 15 at the gate of his oceanfront mansion in the trendy Art Deco South Beach area of Miami Beach.
Cunanan was the only suspect in the killing and was also wanted for the murders of four other men.
Family relatives said Andrew was one of Modesto's four children by his first wife, who lives in the United States.
Modesto described his son as intelligent and "discriminating as far as taste goes."
The elder Cunanan gave the interview before police confirmed that the man they found dead after storming a house boat in Miami Beach was his son.

Police chief Richard Barreto told a pre-dawn news conference that the thumbprint of a man found dead on Wednesday after a four-hour police siege matched that of Cunanan. He could not confirm Cunanan committed suicide but said police had no suspects in his death.
"I'd have my doubts until confirmed by positive identification by the FBI. But I don't have the gut feel it was really him," Modesto Cunanan had said earlier.
Asked if his son had any identifying marks on him, the father recalled a faint scar "the size of a quarter" on his outer thigh.
"No, no, he had a bevy of girlfriends," he said, laughing, when asked if his son was gay. "No way, I raised the boy from the cradle, so I should know."
Police have described Cunanan as a homosexual prostitute.
Barbara Cunanan Carlos, Modesto's sister, said his brother's family was religious.
"I couldn't believe this happened. He was a nice boy and he was very quiet. The family was very religious and they would go to church together," Carlos told Reuters.
She recalled Cunanan was an altar boy when he was growing up in the United States.

"They had a good family. Modesto took care of them well. Their children were studying in exclusive schools and the mother was very religious. She would go to church every morning. It was a beautiful family," the aunt said.
Modesto's house was deserted on Thursday and neighbours said he had left with a female companion a week ago.
